meta.title: Question and Insight Register: control layer
meta.purpose: Open matters, decisions, dated issues, follow-up actions, routing and the identifier crosswalk that sit around the team's Question and Insight Register (the SharePoint list). crosswalkNote: Two ID schemes exist today: the list's Q001 to Q089 (one per question) and V9's QIR-2026-001 to 010 (one per open matter). GOV-004 (one QIR ID across systems) was approved on 15 Nov 2026; this is how the page applies it (the mapping itself is M): keep Q numbers as the single question ID, call V9's records OM-01 to OM-10 with the old ID kept as an alias, and number new items in the list's sequence when they are entered (N-01 becomes the next free Q number). Applied 15 Nov 2026 for new items only: N-01 to N-10 are now Q090 to Q099. Open matters and decisions keep their IDs and are linked from the register's Open matter and Decision IDs columns.

operatingModel.principle: Ask once, record once, resolve once, then reuse the approved answer everywhere.
prompts: Log the question, query, issue, idea or insight once
Check for duplicates first; use clear, concise wording; include context; tag theme and urgency; attach links
Send it to the right forum and owner
What type is it? Which forum should handle it? Assign an owner and specialists; set an expected response date
Monitor progress in the register; follow up if overdue; link to Jira, RAID or milestones; keep the asker informed
Publish the answer so it can be reused
Once approved, publish it in the FAQ, playbook or guidance; link back to the QIR ID; notify interested stakeholders
Capture key learning; identify new or updated guidance; highlight training or capability gaps; close the record (or mark superseded)
ecosystem: Register view: Audit findings to confirm
Assurance of the controls and the audit
Run log of the controls and the audit
Work that needs people or approvals
Jira (MGMT, XDMH): keys in the register's Jira keys column
FAQs, playbooks, interpretation register: linked from Canonical answer
Not connected; add the QIR ID by hand
rhythm: Record the exact question, context and channel; check for duplicates; create or reuse the QIR ID.
Acknowledge: show the ID, name the route and say when the next update comes. Stamp Acknowledged on.
Triage: type, impact, urgency, evidence, best forum, accountable owner and delivery owner. Stamp Triaged on.
Record authority, evidence, conditions, effective date and affected artefacts. Working positions stay visibly unapproved.
Link the answer; update Jira, Planner or RAID; publish reusable content; record whether the matter is resolved.
Review repeated themes, ageing, response time, open dependencies, content gaps, learning needs and whether answers worked.

how: Each Monday the scheduled refresh pulls the register in your browser, rebuilds the live register (checks LR-01 to LR-07) and runs the operating controls in the browser (OC-01 to OC-14). Only the name-free result leaves the browser, and its checksum must reproduce before it is published (CT-01 to CT-05).

The cross-platform sweep (mail, Teams, Knowledge Hub, Jira, Slack, Viva Engage) enters new questions in the register and records corrections as findings for the triage chair. It never changes a status.
The audit is held to its own controls: OC-12 (findings dealt with within 5 working days) and OC-13 (the audit is current and every channel is covered).
Every run is logged in the DAM Automation Health Log, and each control and the audit itself carry their latest result in the DAM Assurance Index.

drafts.subject: Re: DVLA test CDA submission: route for agencies and arm's-length bodies (ref Q084)
drafts.body:
Thank you for your test submission, which we have received, and for checking the route with DfT.

On whether agencies and arm's-length bodies submit directly or through their parent department: we are not prescriptive. You can send your own return, or be included in one combined return from DfT, whichever is easier, provided DfT knows about every return from its agencies and arm's-length bodies and coordinates them.

Please agree the route with your DfT coordinator and let us know which you choose. Feedback on the assets in your test submission will follow separately.

Your reference for this question is Q084.

Government Data Directorate

drafts.subject: Re: DAM Policy return: contact, timescales and template (ref Q097)
drafts.body:
Thank you for your questions, and I am sorry for the delay in replying.

Contact: we do not appoint a contact inside HS2 Ltd; that is for HS2 to decide. For the return itself, your route is DfT's DAM Policy coordinator, who coordinates returns from DfT's arm's-length bodies. You can send your own return or be included in one combined DfT return, whichever is easier, provided DfT knows about it.

Template and timescales: please use version 3 of the baseline return template. The return is due by the end of January.

Your reference for this question is Q097.
